channel.title: AI Retirement Income Planner Blog
channel.description: Practical retirement income planning articles from WebNomad Studio.

item.title: What Is Retirement Income Planning? A Plain Definition
item.description: Retirement income planning is the work of turning what you saved into a monthly income that survives taxes, healthcare costs, inflation, and a long life. Here is what it covers, how it differs from saving for retirement, and when it starts.

item.title: State Taxes in Retirement: How Your State Changes the Net Income
item.description: Most retirement calculators model federal tax and stop. State tax can move net income by thousands a year, and states treat Social Security, pensions, and IRA withdrawals very differently. Here is what to look up, and how to put it into a plan.

item.title: Am I Ready To FIRE? Six Things Your FIRE Number Cannot See
item.description: Your FIRE number tells you whether you can stop. It cannot see the 59 and a half wall, health cover before 65, tax, sequence risk over fifty years, or Social Security arriving twenty years later. Here is how to check the years that follow.

item.title: Annual Retirement Plan Review Checklist
item.description: Use this annual retirement plan review checklist to update balances, income, spending, taxes, healthcare, RMDs, Social Security, withdrawals, and stress-test scenarios.

item.title: How Municipal Bond Interest Raises the Tax on Your Social Security
item.description: Municipal bond interest is free of federal income tax, but it still counts toward the income test that decides how much of your Social Security is taxable. In one worked example, $30,000 of tax-free interest turned a $0 tax bill into $1,645.

item.title: Where to Enter Social Security, SSDI, Pensions and Disability Income
item.description: Social Security, SSDI, a private disability policy and an employer pension are not the same thing, and putting one in the wrong place changes your tax bill and your healthcare costs. Here is which box each type of income belongs in, and why it matters.

item.title: Retirement Plan Guardrails: The Warnings That Keep a Plan Honest
item.description: Retirement income has hard edges — ACA subsidy cliffs, IRMAA thresholds, RMD minimums, an account hitting zero. Guardrails are the badges and warnings that flag an edge before you cross it. Here is what each one means and how to read them.

item.title: How to Set Up a Retirement Income Plan: A Step-by-Step Planner Guide
item.description: A step-by-step walkthrough for setting up your first retirement income plan in the AI Retirement Income Planner, from the setup wizard and starting balances to fine-tuning income across five phases.

item.title: How to Save, Load, and Compare Retirement Scenarios Side by Side
item.description: A step-by-step guide to saving retirement plans, reloading them later, and comparing scenarios side by side, using saved-plan slots and JSON export in the AI Retirement Income Planner.

item.title: Taxes, ACA Subsidies, and Healthcare in Early Retirement: How Income Choices Change the Cost
item.description: In early retirement, where you draw income from decides your taxes, your ACA subsidies, and your Medicare costs. Here is how the AI Retirement Income Planner models MAGI, the ACA cliff, cost-sharing reductions, and IRMAA, phase by phase.

item.title: When to Take Social Security: How to Model 62 vs 67 vs 70 in Your Plan
item.description: How to model Social Security claiming ages (62, 67, and 70) in the AI Retirement Income Planner, using the SS Optimizer and phased withdrawals, including the surprising way claiming age interacts with your portfolio.

item.title: Drawdown Strategies and Stress Tests: How to Know Your Retirement Number Is Safe
item.description: How to pressure-test a retirement plan from six angles using the Drawdown strategies tab and the stress test in the AI Retirement Income Planner, from the 4% rule and guardrails to Monte Carlo.

item.title: The Six One-Click AI Prompts in the Retirement Planner (and How to Apply the Proposals)
item.description: A hands-on walkthrough of the six built-in AI prompts in the AI Retirement Income Planner, what each one checks, how to read the answers, and how to apply the AI's proposed changes with one click.

item.title: How to Keep Your Retirement Plan's Tax Rates Current in Two Minutes
item.description: Tax brackets, poverty levels, IRMAA thresholds, and the Social Security COLA change every year. Here is how to refresh all of them in the AI Retirement Income Planner in about two minutes.

item.title: The Multi-Year Roth Conversion Optimizer: Plan Your Conversions Year by Year
item.description: A walkthrough of the Multi-Year Roth Conversion Optimizer: how it maps your conversion window, respects the ACA and IRMAA cliffs, compares six strategies, and produces a year-by-year conversion calendar.

item.title: Retirement Planning Case Studies: Early Retirees, Expats, and Digital Nomads
item.description: Three worked retirement case studies, an early retiree before 59.5, a US expat in Southeast Asia, and a digital nomad, showing how each situation is modeled in the AI Retirement Income Planner.

item.title: How to Prepare for Retirement: Building an Income Plan for the Next 30 Years
item.description: You spent decades learning how to earn an income. Preparing for retirement means learning how to turn what you saved into one. Here is what a retirement income plan has to cover, and how to build one you can question.

item.title: How Taxes Change the Shape of Retirement Income (Brackets, RMDs, Roth)
item.description: Two retirees with the same gross income can keep very different amounts. This is why taxes are part of the retirement income plan, not an afterthought: cash flow versus taxable income, bracket space, Social Security taxation, RMDs, Roth conversions, and how the planner shows it all.

item.title: How Healthcare Costs Move With Income in Retirement (ACA and IRMAA)
item.description: Before 65, extra income can shrink your ACA subsidies and cost-sharing help. After 65, it can trigger IRMAA surcharges on Medicare. Here is why healthcare belongs inside the income plan, how MAGI links the two, and how the planner shows it phase by phase.

item.title: Inflation and Real Retirement Income: Nominal vs Real, COLA, and the Floor
item.description: A plan can show rising dollars and falling spending power at the same time. Here is why real income, measured in today's money, is the number that tells you what retirement will actually feel like, and how the planner shows it phase by phase.

item.title: How to Check a Retirement Plan From Several Angles (Plan Health)
item.description: A retirement plan can look strong from one angle and weak from another. Here is why no single number tells the whole story, the angles worth checking, and how a tiered Plan Health review turns a wall of numbers into a short list of things to look at.

item.title: Comparing Retirement Withdrawal Strategies (4%, VPW, Guardrails, Buckets)
item.description: The 4% rule, VPW, guardrails, buckets, and floor-and-upside each answer the withdrawal question differently. Here is how the main strategies work, how to read a comparison without just chasing the highest income, and how the planner compares them against your own plan.

item.title: Asking Better Retirement Questions and Reviewing Your Plan With AI
item.description: A retirement plan gets more useful when you know what to ask it. Here is how to turn broad questions into specific, phase-based ones, and how an optional AI review, built on your own plan numbers, can help you find the weak spots and weigh the trade-offs.

item.title: Keeping a Retirement Plan Current: Annual Review and Replan From Today
item.description: A retirement plan is a working model, not a one-time document. Here is a practical annual-review habit, what to update first, why saving versions matters, and how replanning from today re-anchors an old projection to where you actually are.

item.title: Your First Retirement Planning Session: Build a Baseline Step by Step
item.description: The goal of a first planning session is not a perfect plan. It is a clear baseline you can review. Here is a practical step-by-step: gather your inputs, build and read the baseline, save it, then review and improve one change at a time.

item.title: Retirement Plan Case Study: From a Rough Estimate to a Reviewed Plan
item.description: A worked example of the whole framework: a single 62-year-old with $605,000 who wants $4,500 a month. We take a rough estimate through phases, taxes, healthcare, ending balances, Plan Health, better questions, and saved scenarios.

item.title: 50+ Questions to Ask Your Retirement Plan (A Review Checklist)
item.description: A structured checklist of over fifty questions to ask your own retirement plan, grouped by timeline, income, taxes, healthcare, account order, Social Security, Roth conversions, withdrawal strategy, stress tests, and annual review.

item.title: Silver ACA Plan Before 65: How Cost-Sharing Reductions Save Money
item.description: Before Medicare, a Silver ACA plan can unlock cost-sharing reductions that slash your deductible and out-of-pocket maximum, often worth thousands a year. Here is how CSR works, the income band that matters, and how the planner helps you stay in it.

item.title: The Widow's Tax Cliff: Survivor Benefits and Retirement Planning
item.description: When one spouse dies, the household keeps only the larger Social Security check and the survivor moves to single-filer taxes. Here is how the widow's tax cliff works, how to plan ahead for it, and where a survivor's income goes in a plan.

item.title: Retirement Income Is a Timeline: How to Plan in Phases
item.description: Retirement is not one long, uniform period. It is a timeline with turning points at 62, 65, 67, and beyond. Here is how to plan retirement income phase by phase, and how the planner builds that timeline for you.

item.title: Retirement Income: Gross vs Net vs Real (and Reliable vs Flexible)
item.description: A single monthly income target is a starting point, not a plan. Here is how to break it into gross, net, and real income, separate reliable income from flexible withdrawals, and see what your money will actually buy.

item.title: Retirement Ending Balance: The Number That Carries the Plan Forward
item.description: A retirement plan has two jobs: produce income now and leave enough for the next phase. Here is why the ending balance is the number that links your phases together, how to read it by account type, and how the planner shows it.

item.title: How to Compare Two Retirement Plans with AI
item.description: The AI Retirement Income Planner can now compare two saved retirement plans side by side and have AI explain why they differ. Here is how the Ask AI about this comparison button works, what it sends, and how to read the answer.

item.title: Build a Retirement Plan You Can Question (Not Just One Number)
item.description: A single savings total or a "probability of success" score can't answer the real retirement questions. Here is why a retirement income plan should be a working model you can question, test, and improve, and how to build one.

item.title: How an AI Co-Pilot Can Explain a Retirement Plan
item.description: An AI co-pilot can explain retirement plan output, summarize scenarios, clarify Plan Health items, and prepare questions, but calculator math and user review still matter.

item.description: Claiming Social Security at 62 gives income sooner, but waiting can raise monthly benefits. Learn what to model before choosing a claiming age.

item.description: Part-time work in retirement can reduce withdrawals, affect Social Security benefits, change taxes, influence ACA subsidies, and alter Medicare IRMAA planning.
